thread:
Priya K (Support): Hey team — customer BrightCart reported a sharp drop in output quality for model redwood-v2.3-quant in eu-west-1 after last night's rollout. They say the model started hallucinating pricing and truncating product descriptions. Request IDs: r-9891c, r-9898f. Can someone triage? :warning:

Alex Chen: Thanks Priya. Any repro prompt or sample payload we can run locally? Is this isolated to eu-west?

Priya K (Support): Yes, just eu-west so far. Customer provided this minimal repro. They call with temperature=0.2, max_tokens=120. Payload:

```json
{"model":"redwood-v2.3-quant","input":"Generate short product description and price for SKU 1234","temperature":0.2,"max_tokens":120}
```

Priya K (Support): They also attached the two request IDs and timestamp window 2024-05-06T03:12:xxZ. Behavior: previous model (v2.2) returned "Price: $19.99" and full 3-line desc. Now it returns "Price: $1999" or sometimes just "N/A" and cuts off mid-sentence.

Jordan Patel: :eyes: region-only regressions usually mean rollout config or hardware kernel path. Was quantized int8 enabled for eu-west? Check rollout metadata.

DeployBot: rollout redwood-v2.3-quant -> region eu-west-1; rollout_id=rl-20240506-002; percent=100; commit=afe3b1c; quant_profile=dynamic-int8; started=2024-05-06T02:50Z

Kyle R (oncall): Copying logs from rq r-9891c:

```
[2024-05-06T03:12:05Z] request r-9891c model=redwood-v2.3-quant region=eu-west-1 node=a100-32g-12 kernel=int8-dyn v=afe3b1c
[2024-05-06T03:12:05Z] token_stream truncated at 64 tokens
[2024-05-06T03:12:05Z] output: "Price: 1999"
```

Kyle R (oncall): Noticed node tag a100-32g. eu-west cluster primarily runs A100s; us-west runs H100s. Jordan, could int8 dynamic kernel be non-deterministic on A100?

Jordan Patel: There are known differences in quantization kernels across compute capabilities. The dynamic-int8 kernel we've been using has a fallback path on compute capability 8.0 that uses a faster GEMM with different rounding. It can cause tiny FP differences that amplify in generation for low-temp settings. But hallucinating prices seems large — maybe a prompt tokenization or bad vocabulary mapping on quantized weights?

Sarah M (SRE): I can repro locally with an eu-west node image. Running a quick compare across H100 vs A100 images now. Also checking if the tokenizer version shipped with v2.3 differs in that region (maybe packaging bug).

Evelyn T (CSE): Customer also said they pinned model but not model_variant; are we sure the variant in eu-west is the same binary?

Alex Chen: Good call. Check model binary checksums across regions. Command to fetch checksum: `curl -sS https://internal-registry/models/redwood-v2.3-quant/metadata | jq '.regions["eu-west-1"].checksum'`

Sarah M (SRE): Running checksum now... got `sha256:77a9b2...` in eu-west, `sha256:77a9b2...` in us-west. Checksums match.

Jordan Patel: If binary matches, then it's runtime kernel or driver mismatch. What's the CUDA/cuDNN driver in eu-west nodes?

Kyle R (oncall): eu-west nodes: CUDA 11.8, cuDNN 8.2. us-west nodes: CUDA 12.1, cuDNN 8.4. That might explain kernel selection differences. The quant runtime picks int8 kernels based on CUDA version.

Priya K (Support): Customer is pushing — they want either a rollback or immediate mitigation (route traffic away from eu-west).

Alex Chen: Short-term mitigation: route BrightCart's traffic to us-west or to fallback non-quant variant. We can add a customer-specific routing override. Priya, can you ask customer if they accept short redirects?

Priya K (Support): They prefer immediate rollback in-region if possible.

Jordan Patel: Rollback plan: revert eu-west to redwood-v2.2 (non-quant) for that customer or globally if severity is high. But I'd like to capture failing traces first. Kyle, please collect `token_log` for the two request ids and the raw model logits if available.

Kyle R (oncall): Collected token logs and attached to internal ticket INV-3142. Sample logits excerpt for r-9891c:

```
logits[0..8] = [ -0.12, 3.11, 0.98, -1.4, ... ] // token ids mapped to numeric amounts
selected_token=34571 // maps to token '1999' in vocab -> suspicious
```

Alex Chen: That mapping is odd — numeric tokens should be generated as '19.99' or '19' depending on tokenizer. Could indicate a vocab shuffle in tokenizer pack used by quant path. Check tokenizer package version on eu-west nodes.

Sarah M (SRE): Tokenizer package on eu-west: tokenizer-py 1.4.2. us-west: tokenizer-py 1.4.1. Aha. v1.4.2 was accidentally bundled in the model runtime image for eu-west. It includes a patch that reorders some numeric tokens (weird).

Jordan Patel: There we go. So two contributing factors: quant kernel differences amplify small differences, and tokenizer mismatch causes numeric token id differences — together produce large visible regressions.

Evelyn T (CSE): Can we hotfix tokenizer to 1.4.1 and keep redwood-v2.3-quant? That would be faster than rollback.

Alex Chen: Hotfix plan: build new runtime image with tokenizer 1.4.1, push to eu-west as canary 10% for 30m, monitor evals and customer repros. If green, promote. If not, rollback to v2.2 globally.

Priya K (Support): I've informed customer of plan and they accepted canary if we route their traffic 100% to canary nodes. They want confirmation in 30m.

Kyle R (oncall): Deploying image rti-20240506-hotfix-tokenizer -> canary eu-west nodes (tag a100-32g-canary). Will route BrightCart via per-customer override to canary group.

DeployBot: deploy rti-20240506-hotfix-tokenizer -> eu-west-1/canary; status: in-progress

Sarah M (SRE): Added extra metric checks: token-id divergence (KL between token distributions) and price-token frequency. Setting alert if KL > 0.9 or price-token-delta > 0.5.

Jordan Patel: Also comparing top-5 logits across regions for same prompt and seed helps isolate kernel amplification. If top-5 differs significantly, quant kernel rounding is playing a role.

Kyle R (oncall): Canary results after 12m: BrightCart requests on canary returned correct price format and complete descriptions for 94% of calls. No new truncations observed.

Priya K (Support): Customer confirmed on call they see expected outputs now. They want a postmortem and permanent fix timeline.

Alex Chen: Next steps (TL;DR): 1) Promote tokenizer fix to eu-west stable; 2) Add preflight check that runtime image tokenizer version matches expected model tokenizer; 3) Add CI gate for quantized kernel compatibility tests across GPU families; 4) Draft postmortem. I'll own 1 and 2. Jordan owns 3. Sarah will write the postmortem draft with ops timeline.

Sarah M (SRE): Filing postmortem ticket PM-20240506-eu-quant-regression. Will include timeline, root cause (tokenizer packaging + quant kernel differences), mitigation and action items.

Evelyn T (CSE): Thanks team. Customer very appreciative of quick response. Please cc me on the postmortem so I can share with their engineering team.

Alex Chen: Final note: we should add a telemetry check during rollouts that samples deterministic prompts for pricing/numeric outputs across all regions — numeric outputs are brittle and high-sensitivity.

Priya K (Support): Marking resolved for now, will re-open if customer sees anything else. :white_check_mark:
